title: st done --date on a thread already Completed answers ok at rc 0 and records no date, even a malformed one
body:
Raised by vc on 2026-09-22, re-driving row C6 of the Conflab and Baize holds triage (`intent/history/20260921-triage-conflab-baize-holds.md`), whose evidence for this row was a source read and a transcript from 2026-08-28.

**What was seen.** On the installed pair at c3514e151 (`intent 3.2.0 (c3514e151...)`), in a scratch project under an isolated HOME, every verb run in-process:

- A thread closed today with `intent st done ST0002` reads `completed: 2026-09-22`. Then `intent st done ST0002 --date 2026-01-15` prints `ok: ST0002 already Completed` at rc 0, and `intent st show ST0002` still reads `completed: 2026-09-22`. The stated date is dropped, and the line that reports it says `ok:`.
- A malformed date takes the same path: `intent st done ST0001 --date not-a-date`, on a thread already Completed, prints `ok: ST0001 already Completed` at rc 0.
- The control shows the date arm itself works. On the move from WIP to Completed, `intent st done ST0001 --date 2026-02-02` records `completed: 2026-02-02`, and `intent st done ST0004 --date not-a-date` is refused at rc 1: "`completed` was given `not-a-date`, which this field cannot record: this field records ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`, with no time component".

**What was expected.** A stated date is recorded or refused with a remedy, and never dropped under an `ok:` line at rc 0. `--date`'s own help says "Record this completion date instead of today", and a thread that closed on the wrong day, or closed with no date, is exactly the case where it gets used (Conflab issue 0010 is one).

**Where.** `Facade::set_thread_status_fiat` (`native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/facade.rs:11739-11743`) returns `Outcome::AlreadyThere` when the thread is already in the target state. That return comes before the date arm at `facade.rs:11826`, which is where `on` is validated and written. The early return is itself a ruling, recorded in the comment above it: a self-loop must not re-run the gate, so a criterion added after a close cannot block a finished thread. A fix therefore keeps the gate out of the self-loop. The date can still be validated and written, or refused, without the gate.

**Ruled** (vc, 2026-09-22, under hv's pen, answering ic, who takes the fix). On a thread already Completed or Cancelled, a stated date first goes through the same validation a close uses, so a malformed one is refused and never reaches the gate. A date equal to the recorded one stays "already Completed" at rc 0. A date that differs, or a stated date on a thread with none recorded, is refused at rc 1, naming the recorded date and giving the remedy `intent set <ST> completed <date>`. The self-loop keeps meaning "nothing to do", and `set` stays the one door that restates the field, which its companion issue makes validated and status-aware.
